name: net-a4-udp-transport
title: Netcode A4: native UdpTransport (Windows and Linux) implementing ITransport, loopback integration tests with the A3 channels, and refusal of non-loopback binds without encryption (--insecure-bind)
issue: Netcode design C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md (N1-N15 ACCEPTED 2026-10-20: own UDP layer, no new dependency; fail-closed binds: encryption and auth mandatory on any non-loopback bind, --insecure-bind to override (N4); the handshake and AEAD are A5, NOT here). MERGED: A3 #197 (the n2net core: ITransport, SimTransport, packet header, acks, reliable/unreliable channels, fragmentation; read engine/include/engine/network/n2net/* and docs/netcode.html), A1/A2 (settings/presets, SimulationClock). Read the design sections 2.1 (transport abstraction, 2.1.1 native), 2.1.3 (fail closed like the editor host), 1.3 threat model, 6 (testing) and 7.2 (A4), and the editor host's bind refusal and socket helpers (editor-server/: Connection, poll/WSAPoll usage, fail-closed bind from the earlier security work) FIRST. THIS ITEM IS A4 ONLY. SCOPE: (1) UdpTransport implementing ITransport over BSD sockets / Winsock (non-blocking, polled on the calling thread, no threads), IPv4 and IPv6 (dual-stack where available, documented), bind address/port options, max datagram size 1200 from A3, per-peer identification by address (peers are created on first valid datagram or explicit connect: follow A3's interface for connect/disconnect events), socket errors surfaced as data (never exceptions across the API), proper handling of WSAECONNRESET/ICMP unreachable on Windows UDP (ignore as the standard pitfall: SIO_UDP_CONNRESET), EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR, large receive buffers sized sensibly, source address validation, a hard cap on the number of tracked peers and per-peer state (DoS), amplification safety (never send more than received to an unauthenticated address: A5 adds the cookie handshake; here at minimum the transport must not reply to unknown sources by itself), (2) the FAIL-CLOSED BIND rule: binding a non-loopback address is refused unless the caller passes the insecure flag explicitly (the option name the design gives: --insecure-bind) with a loud one-time warning, and since A5 (encryption) does not exist yet the transport API takes an explicit 'encryption available' parameter that is false today: add tests, (3) NOT built for the web (no sockets): guard with the platform macros so the web and any platform without sockets compile (the library part stays; UdpTransport is native-only), (4) TESTS (all native legs: linux x86_64 Clang/GCC, arm64, windows x3; web only compiles): loopback integration: two UdpTransport endpoints on 127.0.0.1 with ephemeral ports exchanging A3 channel traffic (reliable-ordered, unreliable-sequenced, a fragmented large message) with and without simulated loss through a test shim, peer cap, source spoof/unknown-source handling, truncated and oversize datagrams, bind refusal for non-loopback without the flag (use an address on the machine: 0.0.0.0 counts as non-loopback), IPv6 loopback when available (skip cleanly if not), shutdown/re-bind, Windows connection-reset handling (Windows legs), bounded test run time (timeouts, no flaky sleeps: poll with deadlines), (5) DOCS: docs/netcode.html (the native transport, bind rules, platform notes, limits, what is not there yet: handshake/encryption A5, N2Server A6), docs/testing.html. Nothing builds locally for the engine; CI (12 checks) is the test; expect fix rounds; re-read every edit twice (CMake/YAML/C++ syntax); NEVER run taskkill or kill other processes; verify every docs sentence against the CODE; no attribution lines on commits; GitHub only via the wrapper; your FINAL message must be a real report (PR number, head sha, what you did, deviations), never a single word.
acceptance: UdpTransport implements ITransport natively (IPv4/IPv6, non-blocking, no threads, peer caps, Windows connection-reset handling), not built for web
Non-loopback bind refused unless --insecure-bind semantics are used explicitly; tested
Loopback integration tests with A3 channels pass on all native legs with bounded run time
notes: Reviewer: socket error handling on both platforms (connreset, EWOULDBLOCK, EINTR), no blocking calls, bounded peer state (DoS), amplification safety, fail-closed bind cannot be bypassed by 0.0.0.0/::/hostnames, IPv6 handling, flaky-test risk (ports, timing), web exclusion, docs true, mediums count.
